- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.03 to +0.37 in recent days).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows recent decline (e.g., -0.30 to -0.50 in last 3–5 days).
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; model should not adjust forecast by >10% in 1–2 days without confirming trend continuation.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is significantly lower than forecast 3–5 days later, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to account for delayed reaction.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming sentiment will persist; if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts a spike followed by a sharp drop, reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
